page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-60 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 60 vCPUs and 240 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 30 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 24 MB of L3 cache. It features dedicated CPU allocation and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX512_VNNI, alongside AES cryptography and BMI2 instructions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU extended instructions tests scoring in the top 25 percent. Large-block memory bandwidth is also a strong point, reaching 226.55 GB/sec for read-only operations and 97.28 GB/sec for write operations. However, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the middle 50 percent average. Database operations show strong performance, while LLM text generation tasks represent a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25 percent for both small and medium models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2-standard-60 offers a high density of dedicated compute resources and strong multi-threaded capabilities, making it suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced memory footprint for parallel processing. This server is suited for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and parallelized mathematical simulations, whereas workloads requiring high-speed local storage or real-time LLM text generation are less optimal.
